newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia hopes for deal before NATO expansion.
newsitem.headline: Russia hopes for deal before NATO expansion.

text.p: Defence Minister Igor Rodionov said on Tuesday NATO must reach an agreement with Russia before it pushes ahead with plans to expand to include countries in eastern and central Europe.
Rodionov, echoing comments made by other Russian officials, reiterated Russian threats of an unspecified, "adequate" response if NATO goes ahead with its plans.
"NATO expansion is unacceptable for Russia...without an agreement beforehand with Russia and other states not entering the North Atlantic bloc," Rodionov told a news conference.
Asked what Russia's response might be, he said: "Of course we would take adequate measures."
He did not make clear what kind of a deal Russia would expect from the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation before it expanded.
Russia fears the enlargement of its former Cold War foe to take in countries which were once members of the Soviet-led Warsaw Pact would threaten its security interests.
Rodionov said he still held out hope that NATO would take account of Russia's interests over expansion and come to understand them.

He said NATO expansion would threaten the realisation of the widely-held dream of Europe as a "common home" because many countries would not be satisfied with a security arrangement which he said could create new divisions.
"If Russia, a big European state, is not satisfied, something is wrong in Europe," Rodionov said.
